p: vain words have an end: Which serve for vain ostentation and for no true comfort.
soul were in my soul's stead: I would that you felt what I do.
shake mine head at you: That is, mock at your misery, as you do at mine.
with my mouth: If this were in my power, yet I would comfort you and not do as you do to me.
not asswaged: If you would say, "Why do you not then comfort yourself?" he answers that the judgments of God are more heavy than he is able to assuage either by words or silence.
he hath made me weary: Meaning, God.
company: That is, destroyed most of my family.
wrinkles: In token of sorrow and grief.
He teareth me in his wrath: That is, God by his wrath: and in this diversity of words and high style, he expresses how grievous the hand of God was on him.
cheek reproachfully: That is, has handled me contemptuously: for so slapping the cheek signified, 1Ki 22:24, Mr 14:65
hands of the wicked: They have led me where they would.
archers compass me round about: His manifold afflictions.
upon the ground: I am wounded to the heart.
horn in the dust: Meaning, his glory was brought low.
mine hands: Signifying that he is not able to understand the cause of this his grievous punishment.
is pure: That is, unfeigned and without hypocrisy.
blood: Let my sin be known if I am such a sinner as my adversaries accuse me, and let me find no favour.
witness is in heaven: Though man condemn me, yet God is witness of my cause.
scorn me: Use painted words instead of true consolation.

pleadeth for his neighbour: Thus by his great torments he is carried away, and breaks out into passions, and speaks unadvisedly, as though God would intreat man more gently, seeing he has only a short time here to live.
